### Course description

This course introduces undergraduate students to the use of analytical and statistical packages in economics, with a focus on R programming. It provides hands‑on training in data management, visualization, and basic econometric analysis. Students will learn how to design surveys, handle datasets, test hypotheses, and build regression models, while producing clear and reproducible reports for academic and applied economic contexts.

### Course objectives

By the end of the course, students will be able to:

1.  Install and use R and RStudio for economic data analysis.
2.  Design and manage survey data, including creating questionnaires and codebooks.
3.  Clean, transform, and organize datasets using Tidyverse functions.
4.  Create effective visualizations with ggplot2 to present economic data clearly.
5.  Apply hypothesis testing to evaluate economic questions using parametric and non‑parametric methods.
6.  Perform correlation and regression analysis to explore relationships among economic variables.
7.  Model binary outcomes using probability models such as Logit and Probit.
8.  Prepare reproducible reports with Quarto, integrating code, results, and interpretation for academic assignments.
